q: The doctor is kind and speaks my native language, but the follow-up has felt very minimal: basically just an ultrasound every 1–2 months, with little discussion or guidance. I don't have a direct contact if I have questions, and no one has really talked to me about my preferences about the delivery.
cx: 33 weeks, moved abroad, doesn't speak the local language well.

q: I met a midwife yesterday at the hospital who explained how things generally work there (procedures during birth, etc.), but it felt more like an overview than actual preparation. I still don't feel truly informed or supported. For example, no one has mentioned things like preparing the perineum
cx: Her one hospital preparation session at 33 weeks.

q: When I briefly mentioned it at the public hospital, I felt like it was discouraged or seen negatively, the midwife I saw told me she thinks it's "unethical", so I doubt I would have a choice if I go with the public hospital.
cx: Raising a planned caesarean with the public hospital abroad.

q: I feel so unready for a vaginal birth, of course the pain scares me but I also feel unprepared as I didn't do any exercise my whole pregnancy.
cx: Undecided between birth types, both frightening.

q: Yes I probably was expecting too much, as it was my first pregnancy I thought I would have more support and more guidance. I should have contacted a private midwife earlier, I will do that tomorrow.
cx: Reply after commenters said minimal care was normal.

q: knowing I have the possibility in the last moment is less stressful. But I'm not sure if it's worth the price.
cx: Weighing a private clinic late in pregnancy; no amount given.

q: I thought having my husband with me and our newborn for the night was a must have but when I talked about it with friends/family it's not necessarily the case and that I might actually prefer to be alone.
cx: Shared postnatal rooms at the public hospital.

q: I feel like I’m not ready and I’m scared of how much change it’s going to be. I’m scared of loosing myself or my marriage.
cx: Just found out at about 4 weeks; had planned children later.

q: She said “this is not for pregnancy” 🤣
cx: UK pharmacist questioning her prescribed tablets in front of a queue.

q: I get super frustrated because nothing helps completely and I feel like my oils agitate it so I stopped using them, started taking cold showers, and using unscented lotions since I read that helps. but it doesn’t
cx: 38 weeks, belly itching for two weeks.

q: I have an appt w my ob today but idk if they’d be able to help or would do anything to help. i’m just so uncomfortable.
cx: Low expectations of her OB visit.

q: I don’t remember the last time ive ever been this exhausted, i was supposed to go to the WIC center today and i could not even get out of bed.
cx: First pregnancy, first trimester.

q: Does this exhaustion thing end at any point in pregnancy?
cx: Asking when first-trimester tiredness lifts.

q: the only thing that brings me relief is eating! Eating crap! Anything processed, carbs, crisps, fast food, greasy, you name it! I couldn’t stomach a salad if you paid me. I feel bad for not being more healthy.
cx: 6 weeks, nausea starting; it was bad in her last pregnancy.

q: She accused me of "keeping her from her grandson" and when I told her I want this experience between me and my husband, and that this is really important for him too, to be in a place where he is taking care of his family in the delivery room as my patient advocate, she said "if he really wanted to do what was best for you, he'd step aside and let me take over."
cx: 38 weeks; her mother not invited to the delivery room.

q: I'm now getting guilted frequently on how I don't value how she feels or what she needs and I don't understand what it's like to worry for a child's health yet.
cx: What her mother says about the birth-room decision.

q: Even things as miniscule as me telling her I didnt want to travel long distances with her after baby comes because the newest recommendation isn't to have an infant in the carseat over two hours, she got more upset and started going off about new age parenting and how restrictive everything is.
cx: Mother lives in another state.

q: In the past three or four months, I always seem to be the bad guy, and I'm grieving because this isn't at all what I thought this would look like. She has wanted grandkids for so long.
cx: Relationship with her mother strained during pregnancy.

q: I had her in 2022, im due in June with my second and haven’t had anyone buy anything off the registry. I’m not sure if i should be upset by this or worry so much over it. i’m sure people assume we still have most of our things from our first, but honestly we don’t.
cx: 33 weeks; first-baby things given away or sold.

q: I guess i’m just worried of scrambling last minute to find something and worried about scraping by.
cx: Left the military, job-hunting; husband deployed for months.

q: At wits end - been 2 weeks of fearing every feed.
cx: UK, 4-week-old struggling with formula feeds.

q: It’s so debilitating and can’t imagine months more of this. Doctors not really helpful - chasing another appointment next week.
cx: After a health visitor and GP suggestion only partly helped.

q: How I'm freaking out about MY first experience being pregnant and he's kind of a "know it all" because this is his fourth.
cx: First-time mother; husband has three adult children.

q: He just was like "don't be a hero do the epidural" and wasn't listening to me.
cx: Her husband, a father of three, on her birth plan.

q: Is it too late to change my mind? And will I have to fight for it?
cx: UK, 36 weeks with second, eight years after a hard first birth.

q: She asked if I'd like her to book it in, I said yes please and within 5 minutes I was given the date. 😊
cx: Update after the consultant appointment; contrary to expected pushback.

q: People are supposed to be happy while expecting but why do i feel so sad and lonely.
cx: 22 weeks, far from home country, no friends nearby.

q: My 8 week old will start daycare at 11 weeks and part of me is looking forward to it. I feel horribly guilty for feeling this way and also guilty I have to send him.
cx: Second child 12 years after the first, who stayed home with family.

q: My little guy was also hard from birth which has made me feel like I have no idea what I’m doing vs feeling MORE confident as a 2nd time mom.
cx: Second baby, 12-year gap.

q: We also decided to send him a week prior to me going back to work to let all of us acclimate to the change.
cx: Her return-to-work plan.

q: the daycare dint have a concrete opening then but would in a couple months. This gave me huge anxiety since I wasn’t sure what we’d do in the interim.
cx: Daycare place confirmed only shortly before her return.
